headline: Port St. Lucie City Manager Releases Proposed FY 2026-27 Budget
body:
Port St. Lucie City Manager Jesus Merejo has released his proposed budget for the 2026-27 fiscal year, outlining nearly $975.3 million in spending across all city funds.

The proposed budget represents a 12.12% increase from the current fiscal year, which the city says is driven by inflation and capital projects. The general fund budget is proposed at about $230.6 million, an 8.48% increase, or roughly $18 million more than FY 2025-26.

The city's taxable value is also expected to rise. According to the budget brief, Port St. Lucie's estimated certified taxable value increased 5.45%, from $25.5 billion in FY 2025-26 to $26.9 billion in FY 2026-27, due to growth and property appreciation.

Under the proposal, the operating millage rate would remain at 4.6607 per $1,000 of taxable value. The total proposed millage rate would remain 4.9750, including the voter-approved Crosstown Parkway debt service millage of 0.3143.

Residents could see some fee changes. The stormwater fee would increase by $6, bringing the residential rate to $195. The solid waste assessment would increase to $482.16 under the city's contract with its solid waste vendor, though qualified residential homeowners would receive a one-time credit of either $364 or $64. The city also proposes a 3.5% increase in the water rate, while the sewer rate would remain unchanged.

The proposed budget also includes long-term infrastructure planning. The city says capital improvement projects over the next five years are projected to cost about $1.069 billion. The largest portion is for utility system upgrades, listed at $672.7 million. Other planned spending includes $51.1 million for Walton & One, Torino & Tradition Regional Parks and O.L. Peacock Park, $34.8 million for facilities maintenance, $24.5 million for street resurfacing and $9.9 million for sidewalk projects.

The budget brief also notes that Port St. Lucie's long-term debt has declined from more than $1.042 billion in FY 2009-10 to a projected $765 million in FY 2026-27, a reduction of 26.58% over 16 years. The proposed budget includes a net increase of seven positions in the Utility Systems Fund, bringing the city to 1,550.25 full-time equivalent positions.

City Council will review the proposed budget during a workshop July 22-23 at the Community Center, located at 2195 SE Airoso Blvd.

The workshop will also be televised live on the city's website, Xfinity Channel 20 and Blue Stream Fiber Channel 20.
